newsitem.title: USA: U.S. 1996 prescription sales rise to $85.4 bln - IMS.
newsitem.headline: U.S. 1996 prescription sales rise to $85.4 bln - IMS.

text.p: U.S. prescription drug sales to pharmacies rose 10 percent in 1996 to $85.35 billion, led by sales of ulcer-fighting drugs and antidepressants, according to IMS America.

Glaxo Wellcome Plc's anti-ulcer drug Zantac was again the top selling prescription drug in the United States with $1.76 billion in sales, while Merck and Co's cholesterol reducer Zocor showed the fastest growth, IMS said.
IMS, a unit of Cognizant Corp, provides U.S. pharmaceutical sales and marketing information.
Glaxo Wellcome also led the manufacturers with U.S. sales of $5.80 billion in 1996, followed closely by Johnson and Johnson and American Home Products Corp, IMS America said.
Astra Merck's anti-ulcer drug Prilosec posted the second-highest sales figure, at $1.74 billion, and Eli Lilly and Co's antidepressant Prozac had U.S. sales of $1.69 billion in 1996, IMS said.
Astra Merck is a joint venture between Merck and Sweden's AB Astra.
Sales for Amgen Inc's cancer drug Epogen rose 23 percent to $1.18 billion in 1996, while Pfizer Inc's Zoloft, an antidepressant, came in fifth with U.S. sales of $1.10 billion in 1996, it said.
Merck's Zocor had sales of $1.02 billion, up 78 percent, and another cholesterol-lowering agent, Bristol-Myers Squibb Co's Pravachol, showed a 42 percent increase in sales to $565 million, IMS said.
For manufacturers, Johnson and Johnson had the second highest sales among the drug makers, at $5.26 billion and American Home Products was third with sales of $5.25 billion.
Bristol-Myers Squibb Co had sales of $5.16 billion and Merck again ranked fifth with sales of $5.03 billion in the United States, IMS said.
SmithKline Beecham Plc's antidepressant Paxil posted 43 percent growth, with sales of $696 million, it said.

Other products showing high growth in 1996 included Johnson and Johnson's antipsychotic drug Risperdal, with sales of $542 million, up 49 percent, and Glaxo's migraine drug Imitrex, whose U.S. sales rose 72 percent to $580 million.
IMS said sales of Schering-Plough Corp's allergy medication also rose 48 percent to $657 million.
